t: Concerto: Automatic Communication Optimization and Scheduling for Large-Scale Deep Learning
pb: In large-scale distributed DNN training, collective communication (all-reduce, all-gather, etc.) remains a major bottleneck that existing frameworks address only through hand-crafted, framework-specific overlap strategies tightly coupled to particular parallelism schemes. There is no general, automatic mechanism to overlap computation and communication across arbitrary parallelism configurations.
me: Concerto is a compiler framework that decouples communication optimization from the parallelism strategy. It formulates communication scheduling as a resource-constrained project scheduling problem (RCPSP) and applies an off-the-shelf solver to find near-optimal schedules. An auto-decomposition pass splits synchronous (critical-path) communication operations to create overlap opportunities with computation, without requiring manual annotation. The resulting schedule is emitted as a program that any parallelism backend can execute.
nv: Automatic decomposition of synchronous collective communications combined with RCPSP-based scheduling to achieve computation-communication overlap generalized across all parallelism strategies without manual tuning.

mx.speedup: matches or outperforms state-of-the-art frameworks including Megatron-LM, JAX/XLA, DeepSpeed, Alpa (specific numbers not in abstract)

th: Automatic computation-communication overlap scheduling for distributed DL training

t: GraphPipe: Improving Performance and Scalability of DNN Training with Graph Pipeline Parallelism
pb: Existing pipeline-parallel DNN training systems partition models into sequential stages, ignoring the actual DAG topology of modern neural networks, which causes missed model-parallelism opportunities and suboptimal device utilization.
me: GraphPipe introduces graph pipeline parallelism, which partitions a DNN's computation graph (DAG) rather than a linear sequence into pipeline stages. The system represents the DNN as a dataflow graph, identifies parallelizable subgraphs, and maps them to device groups that execute concurrently in a pipeline fashion. A graph-aware scheduling algorithm determines micro-batch execution order across non-linear pipeline stages to maximize throughput and minimize pipeline bubbles, coordinating across branches of the DAG.
nv: Graph-structured (DAG-aware) pipeline parallelism that exploits non-sequential DNN topology to enable concurrent execution of structurally parallel model subgraphs across device groups.

mx.other: Throughput improvements over sequential pipeline baselines (details in full paper)

th: graph-topology-aware pipeline parallelism for DNN training

t: Enhancing CGRA Efficiency Through Aligned Compute and Communication Provisioning
pb: Existing CGRAs overprovision communication resources (routers consume 44% of power/area in spatio-temporal designs) relative to compute capabilities because each PE is paired with a full crossbar/router that handles peak congestion, resulting in low average communication utilization and wasteful programmability encoding.
me: Plaid proposes a hierarchical execution paradigm based on structural 'motifs' — recurring three-node subgraph patterns (fan-in, fan-out, unicast) in dataflow graphs (DFGs). The Plaid architecture replaces individual PE+router pairs with a Plaid Collective Unit (PCU): three ALUs share a single lightweight local router that handles all intra-motif communication internally, connected to a global router for inter-PCU communication. The Plaid compiler (built on the Morpher toolchain with simulated-annealing-based modulo scheduling) automatically identifies motifs in DFGs, generates a hierarchical DFG, and maps it onto the PCU array using flexible schedule templates that maximize resource utilization. Implemented in Verilog RTL at 22nm FDSOI targeting 100MHz; a 2x2 PCU array has 16 functional units (same as a 4x4 spatio-temporal CGRA).
nv: Identifying three-node DFG motifs (mathematically provable exhaustive structural patterns) and designing a Plaid Collective Unit that handles all intra-motif communication with a single local router, replacing per-PE overprovisioned crossbars to align compute and communication provisioning.

mx.speedup: 1.4x performance improvement over energy-efficient spatial CGRA; same performance as high-performance spatio-temporal CGRA
mx.energy_or_tops_w: 43% power reduction vs spatio-temporal CGRA; 27.7% energy reduction vs spatial CGRA; 42% total energy reduction vs spatio-temporal
mx.area: 46% area savings vs spatio-temporal CGRA; 48% area savings vs spatial CGRA; CGRA fabric 33,366 um2 at 22nm
mx.ppa: 1.22x energy efficiency and 1.25x area efficiency vs domain-optimized spatio-temporal CGRA
mx.other: Evaluated on 30 DFGs from TinyML, PolyBench linear algebra, and image processing benchmarks

th: motif-based hierarchical CGRA compute/communication alignment

t: Vela: A Virtualized LLM Training System with GPU Direct RoCE
pb: LLM training at scale typically requires dedicated bare-metal GPU clusters with specialized interconnects (InfiniBand, NVLink), but deploying LLM training on cloud-native virtualized infrastructure using commodity hardware and standard Ethernet-based RDMA (RoCE) introduces performance challenges from virtualization overhead and suboptimal network stack interactions.
me: Vela uses Linux KVM-based virtualization with SRIOV-based network interfaces to enable GPU-to-GPU peer-to-peer DMA (GPU Direct) across VMs without passing through the host CPU. VMs are connected via a virtualized RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet) network built from off-the-shelf NICs. The system was deployed on NVIDIA A100 GPUs in IBM Cloud, using model parallelism for a 50B-parameter decoder model at ~1500 GPU scale, and insights from 2.5 years of production operation guide architectural recommendations.
nv: Demonstrating that GPU Direct RoCE with KVM virtualization and SRIOV can achieve approximately 80% of ideal LLM training throughput at 1500-GPU scale using entirely commodity, off-the-shelf hardware.

mx.other: ~80% of ideal throughput at 1500-GPU scale (50B param model); ~70% per-GPU FLOPS vs single-VM HPL

th: Cloud-native LLM training on virtualized GPU infrastructure with GPU Direct RoCE

t: EDM: An Ultra-Low Latency Ethernet Fabric for Memory Disaggregation
pb: Achieving low remote memory access latency over Ethernet for memory disaggregation remains unsolved; existing protocols (TCP/IP, RDMA/RoCEv2) are implemented atop the Ethernet MAC layer and incur fundamental MAC-layer latency and bandwidth overheads that are particularly severe for small memory messages.
me: EDM implements the entire remote memory access protocol stack within the Physical layer (PHY) of the Ethernet, bypassing the MAC layer entirely to eliminate its fundamental latency overheads. At the switch level, EDM implements a centralized in-network scheduler operating within the Ethernet PHY, inspired by the Parallel Iterative Matching (PIM) algorithm, which dynamically allocates virtual circuits between compute and memory nodes. These virtual circuits reserve dedicated bandwidth in the PHY layer, eliminating queuing delay and Layer 2 packet processing delay at the switch while maintaining high bandwidth utilization. The FPGA testbed demonstrates ~300 ns unloaded latency for remote memory access.
nv: Moving the entire remote memory access protocol stack into the Ethernet PHY layer (bypassing MAC) and implementing a PIM-based centralized in-network scheduler at the PHY switch to create virtual circuits that eliminate queuing delay.

mx.speedup: ~300 ns unloaded remote memory access latency vs. RoCEv2 (order of magnitude lower); 1.3x unloaded latency at high load
mx.other: comparable to PCIe-based CXL solutions

th: ultra-low-latency Ethernet PHY-layer protocol for memory disaggregation

t: Frugal: Efficient and Economic Embedding Model Training with Commodity GPUs
pb: Embedding model training on commodity GPUs (those lacking high-bandwidth inter-GPU interconnects and PCIe peer-to-peer support) suffers poor performance due to communication bottlenecks: sparse embedding lookups generate irregular, small-sized all-to-all communication that overwhelms limited commodity GPU network bandwidth. This makes cost-effective training on low-end GPU clusters impractical despite their cheap compute for the memory-intensive embedding workload.
me: Frugal addresses communication bottlenecks through a combination of: (1) communication-aware embedding table partitioning that minimizes cross-GPU sparse lookup traffic, (2) compression or aggregation of embedding gradients to reduce bandwidth demand over commodity interconnects, and (3) scheduling that overlaps compute and communication phases to hide latency. The system is designed for the constraint of no PCIe P2P, routing communication through CPU host memory when necessary.
nv: A system co-design of embedding-table partitioning, gradient communication optimization, and compute-communication overlap tailored to the specific communication deficiencies of commodity GPU clusters.

mx.speedup: improved training throughput on commodity GPUs (specific numbers not in abstract)
mx.other: cost efficiency on commodity GPU clusters vs. high-end clusters

th: communication-efficient embedding training on commodity GPU clusters

t: Delving into Topology Representation for Layout Pattern: A Novel Contrastive Learning Framework for Hotspot Detection
pb: Machine learning-based layout hotspot detection struggles to capture decision boundaries across entire datasets and ignores geometric/topological properties of polygons.
me: CLI-HD: contrastive learning framework operating on layout sequences and images; Layout2Seq encodes polygon shapes as vectors within sequences; absolute position embedding replaces standard Transformer positional encodings to capture topology.
nv: First contrastive learning framework explicitly encoding geometric and topological polygon information for hotspot detection.
th: Topology-aware contrastive learning for lithographic hotspot detection

t: YAP: Yield Modeling and Simulation for Advanced Packaging
pb: Cu-Cu hybrid bonding for chiplet integration suffers from yield loss due to overlay errors, particle defects, Cu recess variations, wafer roughness, and Cu density; no efficient analytical model for rapid design optimization.
me: YAP: analytical yield model for W2W and D2W Cu-Cu hybrid bonding accounting for five key failure mechanisms; near-analytical model compared against Monte Carlo simulation; 10,000x faster runtime.
nv: First comprehensive yield model for hybrid bonding enabling rapid design-space exploration.
th: Analytical yield model for Cu-Cu hybrid bonding in chiplet integration

t: NeuralMesh: Neural Network For FEM Mesh Generation in 2.5D/3D Chiplet Thermal Simulation
pb: 3D chiplet packaging with dense Through-Silicon Via (TSV) arrays requires fine FEM meshes for accurate thermal simulation, but traditional iterative mesh refinement is computationally expensive.
me: Deep learning framework predicts thermal distributions from geometric, material, and power parameters. Predictions guide optimization of an initial coarse mesh, bypassing iterative refinement. An enhanced segmentation model identifies critical thermal regions; mesh coarsening reduces elements in non-critical areas while maintaining accuracy.
nv: First neural-network-driven mesh generation eliminating iterative refinement for chiplet thermal simulation, achieving 45× speedup while staying within 0.8% of COMSOL accuracy.

mx.speedup: 45× mesh generation speedup
mx.other: 0.8% accuracy vs. COMSOL

th: Neural-network-guided mesh generation for rapid chiplet thermal simulation

t: ParGNN: A Scalable Graph Neural Network Training Framework on multi-GPUs
pb: Full-batch Graph Neural Network training on multi-GPU systems faces severe load imbalance and high communication overhead due to irregular graph structures and uneven vertex/edge distributions.
me: ParGNN employs profiler-guided adaptive load balancing with graph over-partitioning to mitigate load imbalance, plus a subgraph pipeline algorithm that overlaps computation and communication while maintaining training accuracy.
nv: Profiler-guided adaptive load balancing combined with computation-communication overlap via subgraph pipelining for scalable full-batch GNN training.

mx.speedup: 2.7x vs PipeGCN; 21.8x vs DGL

th: Load-balanced full-batch GNN training with computation-communication overlap

t: IRGNN: A Graph-based Framework Integrating Numerical Solution and Point Cloud for Static IR Drop Prediction
pb: IR drop analysis in on-chip power grids is computationally expensive; traditional numerical methods are accurate but slow, while CNN-based ML methods lose fine-grained topology and PG structure information.
me: IRGNN combines numerical solver (AMG-PCG) to generate rough solutions as ground truth with graph-based learning: treats PG nodes as point clouds, extracts features via graph transformer and novel Neighbor Distance Attention (NDA) layer for distance-aware aggregation, capturing both local and global PG topology.
nv: First graph-based IR drop method that performs per-node prediction (unlike CNNs which only produce coarse maps) while grounding learning in numerical solutions.

mx.accuracy: higher than CNN-based and numerical solvers

th: Graph-based IR drop prediction with numerical grounding

t: Invited: EDA for Heterogeneous Integration
pb: Heterogeneous integration (chiplet-based systems) demands new EDA methodologies beyond traditional monolithic chip design. Chiplet disaggregation, multi-physics analysis, physical design for substrates, and interchiplet communication optimization remain open challenges.
me: The paper outlines four key EDA areas: (1) chiplet disaggregation and system-technology co-optimization methods to map designs onto chiplets; (2) multiphysics and multiscale analyses spanning fast ML-driven early-stage analysis to signoff-quality thermomechanical simulation; (3) physical design techniques for chiplet placement, routing, and power delivery on substrates; (4) infrastructure including chiplet libraries, data formats, and standards.
nv: Comprehensive framework identifying EDA gaps and requirements specific to heterogeneous integration, spanning algorithm-level design decisions through physical implementation.

mx.other: not applicable (position paper)

th: EDA methodology framework for chiplet-based heterogeneous system design

t: Late Breaking Results: Automated Topology Generation for Power Amplifier Designs through BiLSTM-based DNN and Multi-objective Optimizations
pb: Power amplifier (PA) design requires selecting optimal circuit topology (matching networks) and hyperparameters; manual design is time-consuming and requires extensive expertise in RF circuit design.
me: The approach uses a BiLSTM (bidirectional long short-term memory) deep neural network to classify and predict the optimal PA topology for a given HEMT device. Multi-objective Pareto front-based optimization refines the DNN hyperparameters (hidden layers, neurons). The method is validated on GaN HEMT designs, generating PAs with 40 dBm power output, 50%+ power-added efficiency (PAE), and >10 dB gain.
nv: BiLSTM-based deep learning for automated PA topology selection, enabling data-driven circuit design without manual topology exploration.
th: Deep learning-driven automated PA topology generation

t: Differentiable Net-Moving and Local Congestion Mitigation for Routability-Driven Global Placement
pb: Cell inflation for local congestion mitigation can over-inflate or move cells back into congested areas; global net bounding box minimization may include irrelevant congestion or miss actual bottlenecks; unbalanced placement density degrades pin accessibility.
me: Proposes momentum-based cell inflation tracking historical ratios for local congestion; constructs differentiable global congestion function from Poisson's equation with virtual standard cells on two-pin nets for accurate net movement guidance; adjusts placement density around power/ground rails per congestion patterns.
nv: Differentiable global congestion function derived from Poisson's equation, enabling gradient-based net movement guidance with virtual cell abstraction.

mx.other: 40% DRV reduction; comparable wirelength and via count

th: Differentiable Poisson-based congestion minimization in routability-driven global placement

t: Gem5-AcceSys: Enabling System-Level Exploration of Standard Interconnects for Novel Accelerators
pb: Interconnect design for novel accelerators (GPUs, DSAs) is critical but under-explored at system level; PCIe bandwidth limits transformer accelerator performance with different memory hierarchies.
me: System simulation framework (Gem5-based) for evaluating standard interconnects (PCIe) with configurable memory hierarchies (DDR4, DDR5, GDDR6, HBM2); matrix-multiply transformer accelerator as case study reveals optimal configurations achieve 80% of device-memory performance.
nv: Gem5 framework with accelerator modeling for standard interconnect exploration.

mx.other: 80% of device-memory performance achievable with optimized interconnects

th: system-level interconnect design for ML accelerators

t: ChipletEM: Physics-Based 2.5D and 3D Chiplet Heterogeneous Integration Electromigration Signoff Tool Using Coupled Stress and Thermal Simulation
pb: Electromigration (EM) in 2.5D/3D chiplet heterogeneous integration systems is inadequately understood; existing EM research ignores Through Silicon Vias (TSVs) and non-uniform thermal distribution between dies, causing signoff errors and missing critical failure modes.
me: ChipletEM couples electrical-thermal simulation using finite volume method (FVM) for initial temperature and current density in TSVs, finite difference time domain (FDTD) solver for hydrostatic stress (nucleation and post-voiding), thermal migration effects, and analytical TSV thermal solver. Components are coupled at each timestep to simulate interactions between EM stress, thermal stress, void growth, resistance change, IR drop, and Joule heating.
nv: First comprehensive coupled EM simulation framework for 2.5D/3D chiplets explicitly modeling TSV electromigration with thermal effects and multi-physics interactions.

mx.accuracy: 0.61% nucleation error, 2.4% growth error vs. FEM, 17% improvement vs. AFD

th: Physics-based EM signoff tool for 2.5D/3D chiplet systems

t: Principle-based Dataflow Optimization for Communication Lower Bound in Operator-Fused Tensor Accelerator
pb: Design space exploration for tensor accelerator dataflows is time-consuming and lacks architectural insight; optimal memory communication bounds for fused operators are not well characterized.
me: Proposes principles for dataflow optimization that provide communication lower bounds for tensor operators; derives optimal tiling, scheduling, mapping for intra/inter-operator dataflow; introduces FuseCU architecture supporting profitable operator fusion.
nv: First principle-based approach to determine communication lower bounds for tensor dataflows; identifies all profitable operator fusions for memory communication savings.

mx.speedup: 1.33x vs TPUv4i, 1.25x vs Gemmini, 1.14x vs Planaria
mx.other: 63.6% data movement saving vs TPUv4i

th: principle-based dataflow optimization with operator fusion

t: MMDFL: Multi-Model-based Decentralized Federated Learning for Resource-Constrained AIoT Systems
pb: Decentralized federated learning on resource-constrained AIoT devices faces challenges from limited computing/bandwidth, non-IID data, and expensive all-neighbor aggregation.
me: MMDFL uses multiple traveler models performing local training across devices, with adaptive device selection based on data heterogeneity and resource availability. Knowledge aggregation is decoupled from full neighborhood dependencies.
nv: Multi-model traveler architecture enabling adaptive peer exploration in decentralized federated learning with reduced communication.

mx.other: reduced communication overhead, improved accuracy on IID/non-IID data

th: Decentralized federated learning for resource-constrained IoT devices

t: HPIM-NoC: A Priori-Knowledge-Based Optimization Framework for Heterogeneous PIM-Based NoCs
pb: Existing NoC simulators and architecture search frameworks are designed for homogeneous architectures and lack support for simulating and optimizing heterogeneous Processing-in-Memory (PIM) configurations with varied core capabilities.
me: HPIM-NoC implements a joint simulation and search framework supporting heterogeneous PIM cores with accurate latency modeling via NoC transmission delays and pipelines. It uses a three-stage heterogeneous search process based on priori knowledge with a customized simulated annealing algorithm, accelerated by precomputing core PPA metrics and reducing NoC simulation frequency, plus a customized layout algorithm.
nv: Co-simulation framework for heterogeneous PIM-based NoCs with multi-stage search guided by architectural priori knowledge and customized layout optimization to explore the full heterogeneous design space.

mx.speedup: 2.12-2.96x search acceleration
mx.other: FoM reduction: 1.18% (ResNet-18), 16.94%, 37.41% under different settings

th: Heterogeneous PIM-NoC design space explorer with co-simulation

t: On Design Space Exploration of Cache System in Multi-Chiplet Systems
pb: Multi-chiplet systems have complex cache hierarchies spanning multiple dies with varying topologies; existing design space exploration methods (NN-Baton, IntLP) fail to optimize cache subsystem performance or explore the full design space efficiently.
me: Proposes bilevel optimization algorithm that models cache miss rates and network latency as functions of hierarchy and interconnect parameters; iteratively solves two subproblems: (1) cache subsystem optimization and (2) inter-chiplet interconnection network optimization to minimize concurrent average memory access time (C-AMAT) under cost/power constraints.
nv: First bilevel optimization method for joint cache hierarchy and multi-die interconnect co-design that minimizes C-AMAT across chiplet boundaries.

mx.speedup: 39.7% execution time reduction vs Zen 4, 39.2% vs Sapphire Rapids, 25.91% vs IntLP

th: Cache hierarchy optimization for multi-chiplet systems

t: Push Multicast: A Speculative and Coherent Interconnect for Mitigating Manycore CPU Communication Bottleneck
pb: In manycore processors running parallel workloads, multiple cores repeatedly fetch the same shared cacheline at different times, consuming redundant LLC and NoC bandwidth through independent demand requests. The reactive cache hierarchy does not exploit temporal redundancy in same-data accesses across cores.
me: Push Multicast transforms the LLC into a proactive agent: when it services a demand request, it simultaneously pushes the data to other predicted sharers via multicast, amortizing the bandwidth cost of same-data deliveries. A coherent in-network filter is installed in routers to prune outstanding demand requests that match an in-flight push, preventing redundant traffic. A dynamic pause/resume mechanism adaptively disables pushing when contention is detected, avoiding interference between push-traffic and normal demand traffic.
nv: Converting the LLC from a reactive responder to a proactive multicast pusher, coupled with a coherent in-network filter that prunes redundant in-flight requests along the push delivery path.

mx.speedup: geomean 1.02x (max 1.56x) in 16-core; geomean 1.11x (max 2.08x) in 64-core
mx.other: 33% avg NoC BW saving (16-core), 43% avg NoC BW saving (64-core)

th: proactive LLC-to-sharer multicast for NoC bandwidth reduction

t: Mithril: A Scalable System for Deep GNN Training
pb: Distributed full-graph deep GNN training does not scale to many layers because inter-GPU communication volume grows with graph size and number of layers, overwhelming existing graph parallelism approaches which partition the graph across GPUs and require massive cross-partition neighbor data exchange.
me: Mithril applies layer-level model parallelism to full-graph GNN training: each GPU owns a disjoint subset of consecutive GNN layers and processes all graph nodes for those layers. This reduces per-epoch communication by a factor equal to the number of GNN layers compared to graph parallelism. Pipeline parallelism across layer-partitioned GPUs is realized by partitioning the graph into dependent chunks; inter-chunk embedding dependencies are broken using embedding speculation (speculative forward pass). A hybrid scheme combines Mithril's layer parallelism with graph parallelism for large graphs to improve GPU utilization and ensure convergence.
nv: First application of layer-level model parallelism to full-graph GNN training, combined with embedding speculation to resolve cross-layer data dependencies in a pipelined execution.

mx.speedup: Up to 2.34x (avg 1.49x) on InfiniBand; up to 10.21x (avg 7.16x) on commodity Ethernet vs. graph parallelism baseline
mx.other: Communication volume reduction: up to 22.89x (avg 6.78x) per epoch

th: Layer-level model parallelism for scalable deep GNN distributed training

t: Enhancing Large-Scale AI Training Efficiency: The C4 Solution for Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Communication Optimization
pb: Large-scale distributed LLM training across thousands of GPUs suffers from efficiency loss due to (1) hardware failures that are slow to detect and isolate, and (2) network traffic collisions that cause prolonged GPU idle time during collective communication synchronization steps.
me: C4 exploits two properties of distributed training workloads: (1) homogeneous, iteration-structured load means hardware anomalies produce detectable syndromes in collective communication patterns, enabling rapid faulty-component identification, isolation, and task restart without waiting for software-level timeouts; (2) collective communication involves a small number of long-lived, predictable flows, allowing C4 to perform proactive traffic planning that eliminates bandwidth contention among these flows and reduces collision-induced queuing.
nv: Using collective-communication traffic patterns as a real-time anomaly detection signal, treating the periodic synchronization structure of training iterations as a diagnostic oracle for hardware faults.

mx.other: System efficiency improved 30-45%; error-induced overhead reduced 30%; communication cost reduced 15%

th: Collective-communication-driven fault detection and traffic optimization for distributed LLM training

t: EIGEN: Enabling Efficient 3DIC Interconnect with Heterogeneous Dual-Layer Network-on-Active-Interposer
pb: Chiplet-based 3DIC systems using active interposers struggle with heterogeneous and high-load inter-chiplet network traffic patterns because their interconnects are tightly coupled to top-die designs, preventing flexible topology adaptation and causing high latency and traffic congestion.
me: EIGEN implements a heterogeneous dual-layer interconnect on the active interposer: an application-aware switch-programmable layer (AspLayer) for static topology optimization and a dynamic packet-routing layer (DynLayer) for adaptive traffic management. A reinforcement learning (RL)-based path routing framework is trained with a state space covering topology, network, and memory metrics, with reward defined as the product of average packet latency and link utilization. The two layers cooperate to route inter-chiplet traffic with reduced hops and congestion.
nv: A dual-layer active-interposer NoC that separates static topology programmability from dynamic adaptive routing, coordinated by an RL-based framework trained on combined latency-utilization reward.

mx.speedup: Up to 11.21% runtime reduction vs SOTA
mx.other: Up to 67.16% latency reduction, 53.89% hop reduction; scalable from 4x4 to 32x32 chiplets

th: dual-layer RL-guided network-on-active-interposer for chiplet systems

t: TidalMesh: Topology-Driven AllReduce Collective Communication for Mesh Topology
pb: Existing AllReduce algorithms are topology-aware adaptations of generic algorithms (ring, tree) to physical 2D mesh networks, resulting in a mismatch between logical and physical communication patterns that wastes bandwidth and increases latency.
me: TidalMesh is a topology-driven AllReduce algorithm designed natively for 2D mesh networks. It pushes data flows between endpoint nodes in a wave-like (tidal) pattern that aligns with the mesh grid structure, fully utilizing bidirectional links and minimizing congestion. Sparse TidalMesh minimizes the bandwidth overhead of the base algorithm. Collective communication unrolling enables software pipelining by superimposing different AllReduce phases (ReduceScatter, AllGather) so that compute and communication overlap across multiple concurrent AllReduce operations, effectively hiding collective communication latency.
nv: A topology-driven AllReduce algorithm designed natively for 2D mesh interconnects that pushes tidal flows between endpoint nodes to achieve near-optimal bandwidth utilization, rather than adapting topology-agnostic ring/tree algorithms.

mx.speedup: up to 24% AllReduce performance improvement on 64-node 8x8 2D mesh

th: topology-native AllReduce algorithm for 2D mesh scale-out interconnects

t: PIMnet: A Domain-Specific Network for Efficient Collective Communication in Scalable PIM
pb: PIM compute units can only access their local memory; inter-bank communication in PIM systems must route through the host CPU, which becomes a bottleneck for collective communication operations (e.g., all-reduce, broadcast) that are common in many workloads, limiting PIM's scalability.
me: PIMnet is a PIM-controlled interconnection network providing direct connectivity between PIM compute units across banks and chips, bypassing the host CPU. It exploits bandwidth parallelism by allowing concurrent inter-bank and inter-chip communication. The network topology matches the DRAM packaging hierarchy with a multi-tier architecture (intra-chip and inter-chip tiers). Unlike traditional network-on-chip designs, PIMnet is managed by the PIM logic itself, not the host, to minimize hardware overhead and optimize collective communication patterns.
nv: A PIM-controlled multi-tier interconnect that matches DRAM packaging hierarchy and enables direct bank-to-bank collective communication, removing the host CPU from the inter-PIM communication path.

mx.speedup: Up to 85x on collective communications; 11.8x on real applications vs. baseline PIM

th: domain-specific PIM interconnect for scalable collective communication

t: NearFetch: Saving Inter-Module Bandwidth in Many-Chip-Module GPUs
pb: In many-chip-module (MCM) GPUs, inter-module bandwidth is physically constrained by organic substrate or silicon interposer manufacturing limits, and fetching data from remote modules causes bandwidth contention that reduces effective achieved bandwidth, degrading GPU performance on high-sharing workloads.
me: NearFetch is a routing-based solution that exploits data locality across GPU modules on the routing path between a requesting module and remote memory. When a memory request traverses intermediate GPU modules, NearFetch checks if those intermediate modules already hold the requested data locally; if so, data is forwarded from the nearer intermediate module rather than from the distant memory partition. A topology-aware Miss Status Handling Register (MSHR) coalescing scheme records memory address information to support future forwarding decisions on cache misses. NearFetch introduces a new Inter-Module Bandwidth per Access (IBPA) metric to quantify bandwidth waste from multi-hop fetches.
nv: Routing-path data forwarding that exploits data sharing among modules along the inter-module network path, reducing effective hop count for memory fetches without modifying the MCM topology.

mx.speedup: 52.2% average performance improvement (up to 98.1%) for high-sharing workloads
mx.other: 42.6% reduction in Inter-Module Bandwidth per Access (IBPA)

th: Routing-path data forwarding to reduce inter-module bandwidth waste in MCM GPUs

t: Zettafly: A Network Topology with Flexible Non-blocking Regions for Large-scale AI and HPC Systems
pb: Post-exascale and zettascale AI/HPC systems require interconnection networks that support both scalability and non-blocking communication for concurrent jobs, but existing topologies (e.g., fat-tree, dragonfly) lack mechanisms to flexibly partition non-blocking sub-networks to match the small-to-medium job sizes that dominate compute-core-hour consumption in production systems.
me: Zettafly is a two-layer topology family: non-blocking groups (NB groups) at the bottom layer connected by global routers at the top, structured so that any minimally-routed packet between groups traverses at most one global router (low-diameter property). NB groups are sized and configured to match common job sizes, providing non-blocking communication within each group. The paper introduces simple adaptive routing algorithms tailored to Zettafly's structure and evaluates performance, cost, and scalability via extensive simulation against state-of-the-art topologies (fat-tree, dragonfly variants) under HPC workload traffic patterns including multi-task mixed traffic.
nv: A two-layer network topology that decouples non-blocking group size from global scale, enabling flexible partitioning of large networks into non-blocking sub-networks matched to typical HPC/AI job sizes while maintaining low diameter and cost-effectiveness at zettascale.

mx.other: Performance and cost improvements vs. fat-tree and dragonfly under multi-task mixed traffic (specific numbers not in abstract)

th: Flexible non-blocking network topology for large-scale AI/HPC interconnects

t: NetCrafter: Tailoring Network Traffic for Non-Uniform Bandwidth Multi-GPU Systems
pb: Hierarchical multi-GPU systems connect GPU groups with high-bandwidth intra-group links but lower-bandwidth inter-group links, creating severe performance bottlenecks on the inter-group network when traffic is not carefully managed. Conventional GPU communication treats all network flits uniformly, leaving bandwidth partially unutilized while also generating unnecessary traffic.
me: NetCrafter applies three complementary techniques to the inter-group network: (1) flit stitching, which coalesces partially-filled flits traveling to the same destination to maximize bandwidth utilization; (2) flit trimming, which drops speculative prefetch flits that are not yet needed, eliminating unnecessary traffic; and (3) flit sequencing, which reorders flits in the network so latency-sensitive critical flits reach their destinations ahead of bulk traffic, reducing effective latency for the most time-critical requests. The techniques are applied at the network boundary without modifying GPU compute pipelines.
nv: NetCrafter combines flit-level stitching, demand-driven trimming of speculative flits, and priority-aware sequencing into a unified traffic-shaping layer that exploits the non-uniform bandwidth structure of hierarchical multi-GPU systems.

mx.speedup: significant multi-GPU performance improvement (specific numbers not stated in abstract)

th: traffic shaping for non-uniform bandwidth multi-GPU interconnects

t: Topology-Aware Virtualization over Inter-Core Connected Neural Processing Units
pb: Inter-core connected NPUs (e.g., Graphcore IPU, Tenstorrent) require large hardware resources, leading to poor utilization when tasks have imbalanced resource requirements, yet no prior virtualization work accounts for their hardware topology (NoC routing, SRAM-centric cores). Existing MIG-style monolithic virtualization ignores inter-core communication structure and therefore delivers suboptimal performance when multiple workloads share the device.
me: vNPU introduces three integrated techniques: (1) NPU route virtualization redirects instruction and data flow from virtual NPU core IDs to physical cores, constructing a virtual topology over the physical NoC fabric; (2) NPU memory virtualization uses SRAM-centric and NoC-aware address translation to minimize translation stalls and maximize effective memory bandwidth; (3) best-effort topology mapping enumerates candidate virtual topologies and selects the mapping that best balances resource utilization against end-to-end performance for the collocated workload mix. A prototype is validated on FPGA (Chipyard+FireSim) and on a simulator (DCRA).
nv: vNPU is the first virtualization design for inter-core connected NPUs that simultaneously virtualizes routing, SRAM-centric memory translation, and topology mapping to preserve the spatial communication structure of the physical device within each virtual partition.

mx.speedup: up to 1.92x (Transformer) and 1.28x (ResNet) vs MIG-based virtualization

th: topology-aware virtualization for inter-core connected NPUs

t: TRACI: Network Acceleration of Input-Dynamic Communication for Large-Scale Deep Learning Recommendation Model
pb: Multi-GPU DLRM training is bottlenecked by embedding layer communication: the Aggregation collective (sparse, input-dependent gather/reduce across GPUs) cannot be accelerated by existing in-network compute solutions designed for All-Reduce because its data transfer patterns are dynamic and depend on input batch content, not topology.
me: TRACI introduces an in-network acceleration architecture with a novel network transaction design that augments messages with input reuse and output reuse identifications, allowing the network switch hardware to proactively identify and exploit message connections on-the-fly. New switch hardware dynamically discovers reuse relationships between embedding lookup requests arriving from different GPUs and performs in-network aggregation or deduplication rather than routing all data to a host.
nv: Network transactions with embedded input-reuse and output-reuse identifiers that enable smart switch hardware to perform on-the-fly aggregation of input-dynamic, sparse DLRM embedding communication.

mx.other: Communication bandwidth reduction for DLRM Aggregation (specific numbers truncated in abstract)

th: In-network acceleration of input-dynamic DLRM embedding aggregation

t: Evaluating Ruche Networks: Physically Scalable, Cost-Effective, Bandwidth-Flexible NoCs
pb: The standard 2-D mesh NoC topology suffers poor latency and throughput scaling for data-intensive manycore workloads, while prior solutions (concentrated routers, widened channels) rely on outdated assumptions that break under modern streaming-bandwidth requirements and impose significant additional cost. A rigorous, RTL-level evaluation of Ruche Networks as a superior alternative has not been performed.
me: Ruche Networks augment the 2-D mesh topology with uniform long-range bypass links (Ruche channels) that allow non-neighboring routers to communicate in fewer hops, preserving the physical scalability and regular structure of the mesh. The authors implement Ruche Networks at RTL level and compare against 2-D mesh and torus topologies under identical conditions, evaluating network throughput, latency, power consumption, area efficiency, and cycle time across manycore workloads with streaming bandwidth demands.
nv: Ruche Networks retain all physical-scalability properties of 2-D mesh while providing architecturally flexible, cost-effective performance scaling through uniform long-range links that require no structural changes to router or core design.

mx.energy_or_tops_w: Superior power and area efficiency over 2-D mesh and torus (RTL-verified)
mx.area: Better area efficiency than mesh/torus per unit throughput
mx.ppa: Favorable PPA vs. 2-D mesh and torus at RTL level

th: RTL evaluation of Ruche Networks as scalable NoC topology

t: Dynamic Load Balancer in Intel Xeon Scalable Processor: Performance Analyses, Enhancements, and Guidelines
pb: Rapid growth in inter-host networking speed causes bursty, unevenly distributed traffic across CPU cores, leading to excessive queuing delays and service latency variance; hardware-based load balancing with the Intel DLB still consumes significant host CPU cycles to prepare and enqueue work descriptors for received packets.
me: The paper first benchmarks DLB against software load balancers with a microbenchmark suite. It then proposes AccDirect, a system architecture and software co-design that exploits PCIe Peer-to-Peer (P2P) communication to create a direct path between the NIC and DLB, eliminating the host CPU from the descriptor enqueue path. The NIC directly enqueues work descriptors to DLB hardware queues using P2P DMA, removing all CPU cycles from the load-balancing hot path.
nv: AccDirect eliminates host CPU involvement in load balancing by using PCIe P2P to connect NIC directly to the on-chip DLB, reducing system-wide CPU power by 10% while maintaining equivalent throughput.

mx.speedup: 14-50% higher throughput than commodity hardware load balancer at comparable p99 latency
mx.energy_or_tops_w: 10% reduction in system-wide host CPU power consumption

th: CPU-bypass load balancing via PCIe P2P NIC-to-DLB direct communication

t: MeshSlice: Efficient 2D Tensor Parallelism for Distributed DNN Training
pb: One-dimensional tensor parallelism (1D TP) for large DNN training scales poorly because all-reduce communication cost grows linearly with the number of devices. Existing 2D TP algorithms for general matrix multiplication (GeMM) have fundamental inefficiencies: Cannon's algorithm generates high traffic, SUMMA suffers from synchronization overhead, and 2D GeMM with standard collective communication operations cannot overlap communication with computation.
me: MeshSlice introduces a new 2D GeMM algorithm that decomposes collective communication operations into multiple smaller partial collectives, each of which can be issued and overlapped with ongoing matrix-multiply computation on the local shard. The algorithm maps the 2D device mesh such that partial all-reduces along one mesh dimension are issued while the other dimension is computing, hiding most communication latency behind arithmetic. An analytical autotuner searches over 2D mesh shape (rows x columns), GeMM dataflow configuration, and communication granularity (number of slices) to find the Pareto-optimal configuration for each LLM layer and cluster size, targeting TPUv4 hardware with its torus interconnect.
nv: Slicing collective communications into multiple partial collectives that are interleaved with computation, enabling near-complete hiding of 2D tensor parallelism communication latency in distributed LLM training.

mx.speedup: 12.0% faster than SOTA for GPT-3; 23.4% faster for Megatron-NLG on 256 TPUs

th: Communication-compute overlap for 2D tensor parallelism in LLM training

t: Chimera: Communication Fusion for Hybrid Parallelism in Large Language Models
pb: Hybrid parallelism strategies (tensor, pipeline, sequence, data parallelism combined) for LLM training and inference on multi-NPU systems generate a large volume of diverse collective communications whose blocking nature severely throttles compute utilization. Redundant communication operators introduced by combining multiple parallelism dimensions compound this bottleneck.
me: Chimera performs a systematic analysis of communication processes for each parallelism dimension (tensor, pipeline, data, sequence), identifies redundant collective operations that arise when multiple parallelism strategies are combined, and eliminates them by fusing adjacent communication operators during parallelism transformation. It reorders operations and generates a single redundancy-free communication operator that achieves the semantics of the original multi-collective sequence. The resulting fused operator is injected into the LLM computation graph as a replacement for the original blocking collectives.
nv: Cross-parallelism communication operator fusion that detects and eliminates redundant collectives arising from the combination of multiple LLM parallelism strategies, replacing them with a single semantically equivalent operator.

mx.speedup: 1.32–1.58x forward pass, 1.16–1.36x backward pass vs no fusion
mx.other: 1.23–7.06x network bandwidth speedup

th: Communication fusion to eliminate redundant collectives in hybrid LLM parallelism

t: FRED: A Wafer-scale Fabric for 3D Parallel DNN Training
pb: Current wafer-scale interconnect topologies (e.g., 2D mesh) lack the flexibility to simultaneously support tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism in DNN training, causing collective communications to contend for shared links and inflating training time.
me: FRED introduces a distributed on-wafer topology built from tiny microswitches interconnecting accelerator chiplets on the wafer. The microswitches form a reconfigurable, nonblocking network that can route collective communications (all-reduce, all-to-all) between arbitrary subsets of chiplets without interference. In-switch collective support allows reduction operations to be partially executed at intermediate network nodes, reducing traffic volume. This topology is tailored so that different parallelism dimensions (data, tensor, pipeline) map to non-overlapping logical groups with dedicated bandwidth.
nv: Distributing microswitches across the wafer to create a reconfigurable, nonblocking on-wafer fabric that supports in-switch collective operations for arbitrary accelerator subgroup communications.

mx.speedup: 1.34-1.87x end-to-end training time improvement over 2D Mesh wafer-scale baseline (ResNet-152: 1.76x, Transformer-17B: 1.87x, GPT-3: 1.34x, Transformer-1T: 1.4x)

th: reconfigurable wafer-scale network-on-wafer for hybrid parallel DNN training

t: DiTile-DGNN: An Efficient Accelerator for Distributed Dynamic Graph Neural Network Inference
pb: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks (DGNNs) combine GNN and RNN computations over evolving graph snapshots, creating combinatorial challenges of heterogeneous operator types, intra- and inter-snapshot data dependencies, redundant data across snapshots, and load imbalance that prevent efficient parallel scaling.
me: DiTile-DGNN uses a redundancy-free parallelism framework that analytically identifies snapshot-level data overlap and eliminates redundant computation while minimizing inter-node communication complexity. A workload-balance optimizer removes synchronization barriers between snapshots. A reconfigurable accelerator architecture with flexible interconnect dynamically adapts to support multiple DGNN dataflows (GNN aggregation, RNN recurrence, and their combination) without hardware redesign.
nv: A redundancy-free parallelism strategy that jointly eliminates inter-snapshot data redundancy and minimizes communication complexity in distributed DGNN execution.

mx.speedup: 23.2-56.1% execution time reduction vs. ReaDy, DGNN-Booster, RACE, MEGA

th: distributed DGNN accelerator with redundancy elimination

t: Cramming a Data Center into One Cabinet, a Co-Exploration of Computing and Hardware Architecture of Waferscale Chip
pb: Current wafer-scale data center architectures waste integration density due to uncoordinated resource allocation between compute and memory dies, and lack co-optimization of system area across chiplet configurations, preventing optimal performance within physical and cost constraints.
me: The paper develops a wafer-scale single-cabinet data center model with configurable on-chip memory dies and a vertically stacked hardware architecture. On this model, Titan is an automated exploration framework that establishes parameter dependencies between intra-chip (tile sizing, SRAM capacity) and inter-chip (die-to-die interconnect, stacking) design variables. Titan integrates vertical area constraints, physical limit pre-checks, and a suite of reliability prediction models to prune infeasible configurations and accelerate the design cycle.
nv: An automated co-exploration framework (Titan) that jointly optimizes computing architecture (parallelism strategy, operator mapping) and hardware architecture (chiplet layout, memory stacking) for wafer-scale systems under physical and reliability constraints.

mx.other: integration density and cost metrics; specific numbers not given in abstract

th: wafer-scale chip co-exploration for LLM data centers

t: LEGOSim: A Unified Parallel Simulation Framework for Multi-chiplet Heterogeneous Integration
pb: Simulating heterogeneous multi-chiplet systems (e.g., CPU+GPU+CIM chiplets integrated on an interposer) is not supported by existing simulators (gem5, GPGPU-Sim) because they lack modular composition of heterogeneous chiplet models and suffer from prohibitive synchronization overhead in parallel simulation—per-cycle global synchronization can waste up to 99.9% of simulation time on barrier overhead.
me: LEGOSim wraps individual chiplet simulators (open-source or proprietary) as parallel OS processes called 'simlets', each advancing independently using a PDES (parallel discrete event simulation) approach. An on-demand synchronization protocol uses adaptive time quanta and non-global fencing: synchronization only occurs when a simlet needs to send or receive a message whose timestamp falls within another simlet's current quantum, avoiding unnecessary global barriers. A Network-on-Interposer (NoI) simulator models inter-chiplet communication (latency, bandwidth, topology) and is integrated as a separate simlet. The framework was validated against SIMBA (multi-chiplet neural network accelerator) and a CiM-based accelerator, achieving average errors of 3.79% and 3.94% respectively.
nv: The on-demand, non-global synchronization protocol with adaptive time quanta that allows heterogeneous chiplet simlets to advance asynchronously and only synchronize when cross-chiplet message delivery actually requires it, reducing synchronization overhead by up to 99.9%.

mx.accuracy: 3.79% and 3.94% average simulation error vs. real hardware (SIMBA and CiM accelerator)
mx.other: Synchronization overhead reduced by up to 99.9% vs. per-cycle sync; 66.1% reduction vs. fixed-quantum sync

th: parallel simulation framework for heterogeneous multi-chiplet systems

t: A. Delegato: Locality-Aware Atomic Memory Operations on Chiplets
pb: Chiplet-based architectures impose high, non-uniform memory access latencies across chiplet boundaries, severely degrading the performance of atomic memory operations (AMOs) used for fine-grained synchronization; existing solutions (near AMOs and centralized AMOs) either cause expensive cache-line ping-pong across chiplets or introduce coherence misses and require ALUs at the directory.
me: The paper introduces two new coherence transactions for far AMOs beyond centralized: (1) Delegated AMOs, which forward the RMW operation via a new SnpAMO snoop to the current cache-line owner, executing the operation locally without cache-line transfer; (2) Migrating AMOs, which transfer cache-line ownership to the requester using an AtomicLoad request (distinguishing it from a ReadUnique for smarter directory tracking). Five static directory AMO policies (All-Central, All-Migrate, Present-Central, Pinned-Owner, Unowned-Central) and a Chiplet-Aware policy are defined based on cache-line state and chiplet location. On top of this, Delegato is a tracing mechanism where the L2 private cache sets a one-bit reuse_bit in every SnpAMO response; the directory's Predictor Table transitions between Pinned-Owner, Present-Central, and Chiplet-Aware states based on this reuse feedback. Evaluated using gem5 23.1 with AMBA 5 CHI protocol, 32 OoO cores (dual 16-core chiplets), and HeteroGarnet NoC.
nv: Delegated and Migrating AMO coherence transactions that enable the directory to execute AMOs at the cache-line owner without invalidation or cache-line transfer, combined with a one-bit reuse tracing mechanism (Delegato) that transports private-cache locality information to the directory predictor.

mx.speedup: 1.07x over centralized AMOs; 1.13x over DynAMO (state-of-the-art AMO predictor)
mx.area: atomic ALU extension: 2894 um2 at TSMC 7nm (0.11% of Neoverse V1 core tile)
mx.other: Delegated AMOs reduce critical-path inter-chiplet messages from 4 to 2 in pathological cases

th: locality-aware atomic memory operation execution on chiplet architectures

t: TileLink: Generating Efficient Compute-Communication Overlapping Kernels using Tile-Centric Primitives
pb: Distributed LLM training and inference require overlapping compute with inter-GPU communication (all-reduce, all-gather, reduce-scatter) to hide network latency. Operator decomposition is easy but leaves performance on the table; fusing communication into compute kernels is effective but requires expert CUDA/NVSHMEM code that is error-prone and non-portable.
me: TileLink has a frontend and a backend. The frontend exposes tile-centric primitives: producer_tile_notify/consumer_tile_wait synchronize tile-level data readiness; peer_tile_notify/peer_tile_wait coordinate cross-rank tile dependencies; tile_push_data/tile_pull_data transfer tiles between devices; rank_copy_data/rank_notify/rank_wait handle rank-level collective coordination. The backend performs tile-centric mapping in three stages: (1) shape mapping assigns tile dimensions to compute and communication workloads; (2) rank mapping determines which GPU rank computes/receives each tile via affine transforms (static) or runtime lookup tables (dynamic); (3) channel mapping assigns each tile to an NVLink/InfiniBand channel. The backend compiles these mappings to PTX via Triton extended with NVSHMEM primitives, producing fused kernels that interleave compute threads and communication threads within a single CUDA kernel.
nv: Tile-centric primitive abstraction that decouples compute and communication design spaces at the tile granularity, compiled to overlapping kernels via shape/rank/channel mapping; achieves expert-level overlap with ~10x less code than handwritten CUDA.

mx.vs_flux: Performance comparable to FLUX (expert-written library) with ~200 Python lines vs ~2000 CUDA lines
mx.code_reduction: ~10x less code than equivalent FLUX implementation

th: distributed-compute-communication-overlap

t: Balancing Pipeline Parallelism with Vocabulary Parallelism
pb: In pipeline-parallel LLM training, embedding and output vocabulary layers placed on one pipeline stage cause severe computation and memory imbalance, worsening pipeline bubbles and memory bottlenecks especially for large vocabularies.
me: Vocabulary Parallelism (VP) partitions embedding and output projection layers evenly across all pipeline devices. Computations are grouped into vocabulary-specific pipeline passes. Algorithm 1 reduces cross-device all-reduce barriers from 3 to 2; Algorithm 2 further reduces to 1 barrier by combining online softmax with pre-computed partial gradients. VP integrates with existing 1F1B and V-Half pipeline schedules via a generalizable method.
nv: Online softmax optimization that reduces communication barriers from 3 to 1 within vocabulary layer passes, enabling vocabulary computation to be integrated into existing pipeline schedules with only a small constant activation memory overhead.
th: Pipeline Parallelism / LLM Training Efficiency

t: Radius: Range-based Gradient Sparsity for Large Foundation Model Pre-training
pb: Gradient communication in data-parallel LLM pre-training is a major bottleneck. Existing top-k sparsification methods fail with AdamW (causing divergence) and have poor scalability due to allgather operations whose cost grows linearly with worker count.
me: Radius observes that top-k gradient indices are temporally stable after 15-20% of training steps. It reuses previously computed top-k indices for T steps (T=200 default) to enable dense allreduce on only the top-k fraction of gradients (avoiding allgather). All workers use identical top-k indices (since indices are computed post-allreduce), so only the gradient values need communication without index exchange. Gradient correction (mimicking AdamW operations) is applied before index selection to select indices based on effective model updates. Error feedback accumulates non-top-k gradients for compensation at resampling steps.
nv: Leverages temporal stability of top-k gradient indices to replace expensive allgather with dense allreduce on a sparse subset, making gradient sparsification scalable and compatible with AdamW for the first time.
th: Gradient Compression / Communication Reduction for LLM Training
